title: Inspection of the Fwd Engine Mount Drain Line Sleeving and Seals
abstract: On-wing visual inspection of the sleeving and the seals on the drain and vent lines that cross the forward engine mount plane, with the surface condition criteria that classify a degraded sleeve.

sections.purpose: This task gives the on-wing inspection of the sleeving and the seals on the drain and vent lines at the forward engine mount plane.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the engine cold so that the sleeving can be handled. The fan cowls must be on their hold-open rods and the rods must be checked before anyone works under the cowl. One person can do the inspection. Good lighting is essential: the surface condition of the sleeving is the whole of the assessment and a shadowed length will read as serviceable.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the engine is cold and that the aircraft is electrically safe. 2. Open the fan cowl doors and check that the hold-open rods are engaged. WARNING: CHECK THE FAN COWL HOLD-OPEN RODS BEFORE YOU WORK UNDER THE COWL. AN UNSUPPORTED COWL CAN FALL AND CAUSE SERIOUS INJURY. 3. Get access to the mount plane in zones 456 and 462. 4. Clean the sleeving and the line surfaces locally. 5. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sleeving over its full length, with attention to the terminations. Reject a length that shows surface chalking, that has lost its outer coating, or in which the braid is exposed at any point. CAUTION: DO NOT RUB THE SLEEVING TO REMOVE A CHALKY DEPOSIT BEFORE IT HAS BEEN ASSESSED. THE DEPOSIT IS THE INDICATION. 6. Do a detailed visual inspection of the seal D7120112839155 at the line interface. 7. Check the clearance between the sleeve termination and the mount link D7120111938052 against the dimension in the illustration. 8. Do a general visual inspection of the drain nozzle D7120115408026 and of the seal fitting 93PP, and check the duct fitting 9634EN for chafing against the sleeving. 9. Close the fan cowl doors.
sections.close_out: Record the sleeving condition, the clearance measurement and any rejected length on the aircraft work card. Replace the sleeving at this visit if any length is rejected; do not defer it to the next inspection. Confirm that the fan cowl latches are correctly closed and that no tool is left inside the cowl.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. One set of surface condition criteria applies and it is given in step 5.

safety_precautions: Do this task with the engine cold.
Check the fan cowl hold-open rods before working under the cowl.
Put the warning notices in position at the engine.

title: Inspection of the Fwd Engine Mount Drain Line Sleeving and Seals

issue.reason: Inspection rewritten around a hardness reading and local charring, the degradation indicators the fire-resistant material actually shows, with a separate limit table for each sleeving material.

abstract: On-wing inspection of the fire-resistant sleeving and the seals on the drain and vent lines that cross the forward engine mount plane, with the hardness check that finds thermal degradation before it cracks.

sections.purpose: This task gives the on-wing inspection of the sleeving and the seals on the drain and vent lines at the forward engine mount plane.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the engine cold. The sleeving hardness reading is temperature dependent and a reading taken on a warm engine will pass an item that is in fact degraded. Establish which sleeving material is installed before you start, because the two materials fail differently and the criteria are not shared. The fan cowls must be on their hold-open rods and the rods must be checked before anyone works under the cowl. One person can do the inspection but the hardness readings should be witnessed.
sections.procedure: 1. Make sure that the engine is cold and that the aircraft is electrically safe. 2. Open the fan cowl doors and check that the hold-open rods are engaged. WARNING: CHECK THE FAN COWL HOLD-OPEN RODS BEFORE YOU WORK UNDER THE COWL. AN UNSUPPORTED COWL CAN FALL AND CAUSE SERIOUS INJURY. 3. Get access to the mount plane in zones 456 and 462. 4. Clean the sleeving and the line surfaces locally. 5. Identify the sleeving material from the aircraft configuration record and select the limit table: table 1 for the original material, table 2 for the silicone-glass material of MOD-161477. 6. Do a detailed visual inspection of the sleeving over its full length, with attention to the terminations. On the original material look for surface chalking and braid exposure. On the silicone-glass material neither indication appears: it degrades by local charring at the hottest point of the run, usually a brown to black band 20 to 40 mm long on the upper surface, with no loss of coating anywhere else. CAUTION: DO NOT PASS A SILICONE-GLASS SLEEVE BECAUSE IT IS CLEAN AND UNCHALKED. THAT MATERIAL DOES NOT CHALK AND A SERVICEABLE APPEARANCE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF A SERVICEABLE SLEEVE. 7. Take a hardness reading of the sleeving at each of the three positions in the illustration and record it against the table selected at step 5. The silicone-glass material fails by stiffening and the hardness reading is the primary indicator on it. CAUTION: TAKE THE HARDNESS READINGS ONLY WHEN THE ENGINE IS COLD. A WARM READING WILL PASS A DEGRADED SLEEVE. 8. Do a detailed visual inspection of the seal D7120112839155 at the line interface. 9. Check the clearance between the sleeve termination and the mount link D7120111938052 against the dimension in the illustration. 10. Do a general visual inspection of the drain nozzle D7120115408026 and of the seal fitting 93PP. 11. Check the duct fitting 9634EN for chafing against the sleeving and close the fan cowl doors.
sections.close_out: Record the hardness readings against the table used, the clearance measurement and the sleeving condition on the aircraft work card. Replace the sleeving at this visit if any reading is outside the limit; do not defer it to the next inspection. A charred band on the silicone-glass material is a replacement item whatever the hardness reading says. Confirm that the fan cowl latches are correctly closed and that no tool is left inside the cowl.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Pre MOD-161477 aircraft carry the original sleeving and are assessed against table 1, on surface chalking and braid exposure. Post MOD-161477 aircraft carry the silicone-glass sleeving and are assessed against table 2, on hardness and local charring; the table 1 criteria will pass a degraded silicone-glass sleeve and must not be applied to it.

safety_precautions: Do this task with the engine cold.
Check the fan cowl hold-open rods before working under the cowl.
Put the warning notices in position at the engine.
